sources_not_read: AED COP Word 365 guide PDF: the figure images (screenshots, Figures 1–30) were not viewed. All text and figure captions were read via text extraction. The extracted text shows no version or publication date.

ICT Baseline per-baseline pages (document-baselines/01KeyboardDocs … 24ParsingDocs): not read one by one, except 13StructureDocs, which matches the all-tests page. The all-tests page carries the same test text and was read in full. Appendix A (cross-reference table) was only scanned. Appendix B Change Log was not read: the fetch never ran.

W3C technique pages: Examples, Related Techniques and Resources sections were not read, except F1's examples. Title, applicability, Description, Procedure and Expected Results were read for all 27. The WCAG21 URLs serve the current text (page dates run from July 2025 to September 2026), not a frozen WCAG 2.1 snapshot.
Glossary term 'visual heading': there's no such entry in the baseline glossary (searched; this isn't a read failure). The 13.A/13.B Identify Content wording is recorded as a separate entry instead.

citations.quote: all visual headings are programmatically determinable and that programmatic heading levels logically match
headings in the Navigation pane match the visual outline (hierarchy) of the document

entries.reasoning: Each A03 location carries the full outline of marked headings, not just the neighbouring paragraphs. A 'no' from both testers = fail. Skipped levels as such pass (S2 and the 13.B exceptions).

critic_gaps.what: Row 22 (F72, keyboard-character drawings such as a seating plan) has no entry at all. F72 was read but no entry cites it, so there is no Word-document test for row 22, and no ruling on the common case of separator lines built from repeated characters (dashes, equals signs, asterisks).
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a judgment entry from the F72 procedure. Test question: are these characters arranged to form a picture or diagram that conveys information, with no text alternative next to it? Yes = fail row 22. Add a pass entry (or a 'No' example) for decorative separator runs and for typed fill-in blanks (A29/B30). Cite F72 plus Baseline 6.A and the Non-text content glossary entry.

critic_gaps.what: B02 says the picture fails unless both testers answer yes. S3(b) says that when the two blind testers disagree on a D1-D6 location, the location is contested, not fail.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Restate B02 as: both answer no = fail, both answer yes = the yes outcome, split = contested under S3(b). Also add one general rule that applies to every judgment entry (A01 says 'the tester', singular).

critic_gaps.what: Contradiction between entries. B01 fails any body picture with no alt text that is not marked decorative, mechanically, under F65/F38; row 13 plants exactly that state. But B02's yes path and B04 let a picture in that same state pass when it sits behind text or in a header/footer. No quoted tier 2 or 3 test shows that header/footer or behind-text pictures are ignored by assistive technology, and B01 still fails pictures floating in front of the text.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Find a Baseline 6.B or Word-guide quote that treats header/footer or behind-text pictures differently. If there is none, rule the decorative-but-unmarked outcome of B02/B04 a fail under row 13 (F38). If the sources conflict, record both quotes and rule it contested under S3(a).

critic_gaps.what: B35 rules 'pass' on a condition worded as permissions restricting programmatic access by assistive technology. If that were really true it would be an A-level problem matching none of the 31 rows, and S2 makes that contested, not pass. The pass actually rests on the unstated claim that .docx editing or write protection doesn't block assistive-technology reading. Information Rights Management or encryption isn't ruled.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Reword the condition to the stored form only: w:documentProtection or w:writeProtection = pass, with a quote showing it doesn't block reading. Add a contested entry under S2 for a file whose protection actually prevents assistive-technology access.

critic_gaps.what: A14 cites 'W3C technique F32 Example 3', but the source reader reports that Examples sections weren't read for any technique except F1. That citation rests on unread text, and S5 requires a real quote.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Read the F32 Examples section and quote it under 15 words, or drop the citation and rely on the F32 Description and Procedure.

critic_gaps.what: Tier 1 and tier 2 text wasn't read completely. The technique URLs serve the current text (dated 2025-2026), not a frozen WCAG 2.1 snapshot. Examples and Related Techniques were unread for 26 of 27 techniques. Baseline Appendix B (change log) was never fetched. The Word guide's figures (screenshots 1-30) weren't viewed, though guide steps such as 2A, 9C and 10B may depend on them.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Check every quoted technique sentence against the dated WCAG 2.1 technique text, read Appendix B for v1.0 errata, and view the figures for the guide tests that are cited.

critic_gaps.what: Only 13StructureDocs was checked against the all-tests page. The per-baseline pages for tables and meaningful sequence (12, 18) weren't read, yet A16, A17 and A18 cite '12 Limitations' and '12 Advisory' notes. These per-baseline pages may carry extra Word-specific notes.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Read 12TablesDocs and 18 MeaningfulSequence (also 06 Images for cluster B) and confirm that the Limitations and Advisory text quoted matches.

critic_gaps.what: Baseline tests that bear on the table rows were read but never cited. 12.A DataTableRole bears on rows 11 and 12 (F33/F34: data shown with tabs rather than a table). 12.B DataTableHeaderAssociation bears on row 28 (F91). A12 and A16 rely on the W3C techniques, '12 Limitations' and the Word guide only.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add the 12.A and 12.B test wording to A12 and A16, or state that they add nothing for .docx files.

critic_gaps.what: Word 365 guide tests 5B, 9A, 9B and 9D were read but no entry cites them. They may bear on floating-object order (A22, which cites no guide test) and on the table entries A16-A21. A19-A21 cite only S2.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Check each against rows 1, 16, 17 and 28 and cite them where they give the how-to-test steps. Record any conflict with a tier-2 test under S3(a).

critic_gaps.what: Word 365 guide tests 1A, 1B, 10A, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 16 were read but no entry cites them. In particular, no guide test is cited for meaningful-image alt text (B01, B08, B09), colour or contrast (B19-B21), the document language (B22) or the title (B16-B18).
critic_gaps.suggestion: Map each guide test to a row or record that it bears on none. If a guide test treats something differently, such as the file name as the title, record the conflict under S3(a).

critic_gaps.what: Baseline tests bearing on the form and picture rows weren't used. 5.A ControlName bears on rows 20 and 26 (4.1.2 name); B25 cites only 10.A. 6.D ImageText isn't cited by any picture entry. 10.B and 10.E, which cover labels, aren't cited, though B27 is contested on that ground.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Cite 5.A in B25 and B32. Use 6.D for a scanned-text entry and 10.B/10.E for the label-related contested entries.

critic_gaps.what: Several judgment entries in cluster A have no location question type, so D1-D6 locations for them can never reach blind testers: A22 (text box K50/K51 is in the corpus), A14 (letter-spaced word K27), A28 (header text K46/K30), and A30/A31. A03 needs the whole heading outline, but each HEADING location shows one paragraph with only its neighbours' text.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add ORDER, SPACING, HEADER-TEXT and SENSORY location types, or state that D1-D6 contain no such locations. Give A03 testers the full outline of marked headings.

critic_gaps.what: Several judgment entries in cluster B have no location question type: B13 (links; K25 is in 8 corpus files), B19 (colour; K43), B21 (text over picture), B22-B24 (language; K39), B27 (content-control titles), B32 (ActiveX; K01) and B03/B04 (header pictures; K38). The only PICTURE location is one behind-text picture with no alt text, so B07, B08 and B10 (pictures with alt text; K34) are never put to testers.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add LINK, COLOUR, LANGUAGE, CONTROL and HEADER-PICTURE question types, and add PICTURE locations for every picture in D1-D6 that has alt text, or record that none exist.

critic_gaps.what: Every location comes from word/document.xml. A01 lists K46 (all-caps lines in headers) and A12 lists K30 (tab-separated header text) as candidates. No entry says whether text in headers, footers, footnotes or text boxes can be a visual heading, list or tab-column layout. Only B25 names the parts it covers; B13, B19, B20 and B22-B24 don't say whether they apply outside the body.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a scope entry per part (header, footer, notes, text box). Either rule that A01/A11/A12 don't apply to header and footer text, with a source, or create locations for it. State the parts each B entry covers.

critic_gaps.what: Header and footer parts that Word never displays aren't ruled. A first-page header shows only when w:titlePg is set, and even-page headers only when w:evenAndOddHeaders is set; such parts appear in the corpus (K17, K18, K20, K21). B03, B04, B25 and A28 judge content in 'a header or footer part' without saying whether the part is shown.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a mechanical entry: content in a header or footer part that the section settings never display is not presented content and passes (cite S1/S2), or rule otherwise with a quote.

critic_gaps.what: Footnotes and endnotes have no entry beyond the blank separator paragraphs (K06, notes in 23 corpus files). Nothing rules on footnote or endnote content, or on reference numbers typed as manual superscript instead of Word's footnote feature, both common in ordinances and reports.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Rule Word footnotes as such a pass (S2). Rule typed superscript references through S2 (pass, unless a failure technique among the rows names them). State that the link, language, contrast and picture entries also apply in the notes parts.

critic_gaps.what: F2 (rows 2 and 3) is applied only to headings and lists. No entry covers other meaning carried only by formatting, such as ordinance amendments shown by strikethrough for deleted text and underline for added text, or bold or italic marking status. F2's procedure covers these, and it's unsettled whether Word run properties such as w:strike count as programmatic.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a judgment entry from the F2 procedure. Test question: does this formatting convey information that the text doesn't state? Settle with a quote whether run properties are programmatically determinable in Word; if the sources leave it open, rule it contested.

critic_gaps.what: Word-generated tables of contents (TOC fields with dot leaders and right-aligned page numbers) and print-form label and signature lines built with tab leaders aren't ruled. A12 names tab leaders as a sign of a failing column layout, so its judgment would fail every generated TOC.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add an entry ruling a TOC field (TOC1-9 styles, PAGEREF links) a pass as such under S2, and add tab-leader TOC and label lines to A12's 'No' examples, or rule them under F33/F34 with that technique's test procedure.

critic_gaps.what: 'Heading style' is never defined. Unruled cases: the built-in Title and Subtitle styles (no outline level), custom styles that get an outline level from their style definition or from a basedOn Heading style, and Heading styles whose outline level was reset to body text. A09 covers only an outline level set directly on the paragraph.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a mechanical definition of 'marked as heading': the resolved outline level 0-8 after style inheritance. Add an entry saying whether a document title in Title style that works as a visual heading fails under A01.

critic_gaps.what: Headings and list items that aren't separate paragraphs aren't ruled: a bold heading line followed by a manual line break (w:br) inside its paragraph, list items separated by line breaks, and headings or typed lists inside table cells or text boxes. A01, A10 and A11 are tested per paragraph, and locations are per paragraph.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Extend A01, A10 and A11 to visual lines split by w:br and to table-cell and text-box paragraphs, and generate locations for them.

critic_gaps.what: List problems other than typed labels have no entry or LIST question: Word list formatting whose nesting level (ilvl) doesn't match the visual indent, and numbering or bullet formatting applied to text that isn't a list (an analogue of F43, like A02 for headings).
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add judgment entries for each through F2 and F43 with their procedures, or rule them a pass under S2 if no technique names them.

critic_gaps.what: A16 tests only whether the first row has w:tblHeader. Unruled: data tables whose headers are in the first column (Word can't mark row headers), a merged title row above the real column-header row, multi-row headers, and w:tblHeader on rows not contiguous from the top. Also unruled: table alt text or captions (w:tblCaption/w:tblDescription) missing, which checkers often flag.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a judgment entry for which rows are header rows when the first row is a title. Rule row-header-only data tables (possibly contested under S3(a)). Rule a missing table caption or description a pass under S2.

critic_gaps.what: S2 names 2.4.6 descriptive headings (Baseline 13.A) as contested, but no entry records it. The A02 judgment may absorb 'not descriptive' answers. A08 (long heading = mechanical pass) can collide with A02 when a long body paragraph is styled as a heading.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a contested S2 entry for heading text that doesn't describe its section. Make A08 defer to A02 so a long heading-styled paragraph is still judged under A02.

critic_gaps.what: A25 passes hidden (w:vanish) text as such, but HEADING, LIST and COLUMNS locations carry no hidden flag. Web-form boundary markers left by pasted web pages show up among the HEADING candidates. No entry says that hidden or non-printing text can't be a visual heading, list item or column layout.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add an entry: hidden text and form-boundary marker paragraphs are not visual content and pass under A01, A11 and A12. Add the hidden state to the location formatting.

critic_gaps.what: Drop caps aren't ruled. A drop cap (w:framePr dropCap) stores a word's first letter in its own frame paragraph. A14's test counts 'paragraph breaks' typed between letters, so a drop-capped word could be judged an F32 failure, and A22 also sweeps in frames.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Rule drop-cap frames explicitly: pass, citing F32's scope (white-space characters used to control spacing), or judge them under A14 with a quote.

critic_gaps.what: Word's built-in text watermarks are WordArt or VML textpath shapes in the header, not pictures and not header text runs. B03 and B04 cover pictures, and A28 covers header text, so a DRAFT text watermark isn't ruled.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add an entry: a header text-watermark shape whose words appear nowhere else in the document is judged like B03/B04 (row 4, F3, or contested under S2 like A28), with the stored form named.

critic_gaps.what: Legacy form fields (FORMTEXT, FORMCHECKBOX and FORMDROPDOWN with w:ffData), common in older municipal forms, have no entry. No entry says what supplies their name under F68: help text, status text or bookmark.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add mechanical and judgment entries for legacy form fields under rows 20 and 26, with the Baseline 10.A or 5.A test wording on how to read their name.

critic_gaps.what: Template placeholders aren't ruled for contrast. Placeholder text in content controls uses Word's Placeholder Text style (grey, typically under 4.5:1 on white), so B20 would fail it mechanically, and no entry decides whether placeholder text showing is visible text under 1.4.3. Also unruled: MACROBUTTON/FILLIN placeholder fields in older templates, and how B20 resolves w:color 'auto' and theme colours with tint or shade.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add an entry for placeholder text, using the 1.4.3 exceptions as quoted in Baseline 8. Add a pass entry (S2) for MACROBUTTON placeholders as such. Specify how B20 computes auto and theme colours.

critic_gaps.what: Symbol-font characters aren't ruled: w:sym or Wingdings/Symbol private-use characters used as print-form check boxes, bullets, arrows or check marks. Screen readers may read them as unrelated letters. No entry relates them to F71 (row 21), F26 (row 8) or A10's typed-bullet test.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a mechanical entry for symbol-font characters, ruled under F71 or F26 with that technique's test procedure, or a pass under S2. Say whether A10 counts a w:sym bullet as a typed bullet glyph.

critic_gaps.what: Scanned images of text (scanned letters, notices or signed pages) and signature images aren't ruled. S2 names 1.4.5 images of text as contested, but no entry records it. The 1.1.1 question of whether the alt text carries the pictured text rests only on B08's general question, with Baseline 6.D unused.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a contested S2 entry for an image of text as such. Add a judgment entry under rows 19 and 9: does the alt text contain the text shown in the picture? Say whether a signature image is meaningful.

critic_gaps.what: B01's mechanical test doesn't say which element carries the alt text for embedded OLE objects (Excel worksheets shown as images, embedded PDFs or icons), grouped drawings (the group or each member), drawing canvases, or horizontal rules from pasted web content (VML o:hr). Paragraph-border dividers (w:pBdr) aren't ruled at all.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Extend B01 with the alt-text location for each stored form. Rule paragraph borders a pass as formatting (S2).

critic_gaps.what: Three candidate conditions are attached to entries that don't rule on them. C08 (the same link text going to different destinations) is attached to B13, which judges link purpose in context. The 'very short alt text' half of C03 and C04 (a picture that may need a longer description) are attached to B07-B09.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add S2 pass entries for C08, for short alt text and for a missing long description as such, each deferring to B13 or B08 for the row judgment.

critic_gaps.what: Language setup isn't fully ruled. B22 judges a mismatch between the default language and the content, but no entry covers a document with no default language set (no w:lang in docDefaults or the Normal style), says which w:lang attribute counts (val, eastAsia or bidi), or covers w:noProof runs.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add a mechanical entry for a missing default language under row 30 (Baseline 15.A). State which attribute B22-B24 read.

critic_gaps.what: Tracked changes (w:ins/w:del) and comments left in the saved file aren't ruled; checkers often flag them. Web addresses and email addresses typed as plain text without a hyperlink, and internal bookmark links, have no entry either.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add S2 pass entries for revisions and comments as such and for unlinked URLs. State that B13 applies to internal links.

critic_gaps.what: Other WCAG A/AA conditions that match none of the 31 rows have no contested entry under S2: 1.4.11 non-text contrast (chart colours, shape and check-box borders), 2.1.1 keyboard for ActiveX and content controls (S2's own example), 4.1.2 role, state and value for check-box controls (Baseline 5.B-5.D), and 3.3.2 visible labels for form fields (Baseline 10.E). Without these, a checker's claim on them could be ruled pass or slip in as a back-door row.
critic_gaps.suggestion: Add one contested S2 entry per condition, citing the Baseline test that describes it.

critic_gaps.what: Some row entries rest on the W3C technique alone, with no Baseline or Word-guide test for how to check them in a .docx: row 8 (A31 cites only F26; Baseline 7.B is unused there), row 10 (A14 and A15) and row 21 (B33). A30 and A31 also have no candidates, so nothing ties them to the corpus.
critic_gaps.suggestion: For each, cite the tier-2 or tier-3 test (for example, 7.B for row 8) or state that tiers 2 and 3 are silent and the technique's own procedure is the test.
